creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Paste works and copy does not, which for anything involving a terminal is an hourly need. Reading an error out of a pane and putting it somewhere means retyping it.

Two halves, and only one of them is the thing that is blocked upstream.

Making a selection. `SurfaceView.mouseDown` sends a focus request and returns; nothing reaches the libghostty surface, so there is currently no way to drag out a selection at all. This is *not* a_27CTgqqdv. That card is about mouse buttons and motion being reported to the program running in the pane, which needs herdr to expose the pane's modes and is genuinely stuck. A selection is the surface's own - it is made against the grid libghostty already painted, and no daemon has to agree to anything.

Reading it back. AppMenu.swift currently says a pane's selection lives in the daemon where Muster cannot yet reach it. That is wrong for the pinned libghostty: `ghostty_surface_has_selection` and `ghostty_surface_read_selection` are both in deps/ghostty/include/ghostty.h, and the header also carries clipboard read/write callbacks on the runtime config. Worth correcting the comment whichever way this lands.

So: an Edit menu item beside Paste, reading the focused surface's selection, and enough mouse handling for a drag to make one. Selection also wants a visible highlight, which libghostty draws itself once it knows a selection exists.

Open: whether keyboard selection is wanted too, and whether double-click-to-word and triple-click-to-line come for free from the surface or need wiring.
title: 📋 Copy what is selected in a pane
